title: Backup/Restore Toolkit (Redwood Private) — Draft Outline + Assets Needed
body:
Purpose
- Working outline for the operator-facing docs for Redwood Private Day-2 ops: backup/restore + DR planning.
- Capture what sections we need, what screenshots/diagrams we still need, and what’s still unclear.
- Target: publish in redwood-docs + link from Private install/upgrade docs.

Audience (rough)
- Primary: customer operators running Redwood Private (platform/SRE) in VPC Kubernetes and on-prem.
- Secondary: Redwood Solutions Eng + Support + internal on-call.

Doc set structure (proposed IA)
NOTE: trying to keep “concepts” separate from “runbooks”.

A) Overview / landing page
1. “Backup & Restore for Redwood Private” (conceptual overview)
   - What the toolkit is / isn’t
   - Supported deployment modes
     - Private in VPC (managed K8s)
     - On-prem (including restricted network / air-gapped)
   - High-level flow diagram: backup create -> store -> verify -> restore plan -> restore execute -> validate
   - Links to runbooks + DR planning + troubleshooting
   - Ownership/escalation: customer operator vs Redwood SE/SRE

B) Concepts (how it works)
2. “What data/state is protected?”
   - Control plane DB(s) (Postgres) + PITR notes
   - Object storage (model artifacts, logs, etc.)
   - Config/policy data
   - Secrets/certs (what we do vs what customer manages)
   - Integrations (KMS/HSM, SIEM/audit export)
   - Explicit callouts: what is NOT covered (e.g., GPU node images, underlying cluster config)

3. “Backup architecture + storage targets”
   - Components: rw-private-dr CLI, k8s Jobs/CronJobs, credentials, encryption
   - Storage backends: S3 / GCS / Azure Blob / NFS / minio
   - Compatibility matrix (VPC vs on-prem)
   - Credential patterns
     - IRSA / workload identity (cloud)
     - static creds + sealed secret (on-prem)
   - Concurrency + performance considerations
     - don’t overlap backups
     - backup windows
     - DB contention and scheduling guidance

4. “Encryption & key handling”
   - What is encrypted, where, and with which keys
   - SSE-S3 / KMS vs client-side encryption (what we recommend)
   - Key ownership boundary (“Redwood should never need plaintext key material”)
   - Logging redaction expectations
   - Evidence requirements for compliance (SOC2/ISO-ish)

C) Operator guides / tasks
5. “Quickstart: enable scheduled backups”
   - Prereqs checklist
     - storage target reachable from cluster
     - credentials/IAM policies in place
     - required helm values / installer config
     - optional: VPC endpoints for S3
   - Configure
     - Helm values (backup window, timeouts, retries, retention)
     - Validate: dry-run or “backup verify”
   - Verify success + where artifacts land

6. Runbook: “Create and verify a backup” (manual)
   - When to do this (before upgrades, before risky changes, before restore drills)
   - Commands
     - rw-private-dr backup create …
     - rw-private-dr backup verify …
   - Expected output
   - Common errors

7. Runbook: “Restore in place”
   - Maintenance mode (block writes)
   - Restore sequencing (control plane first)
   - Postgres restore + PITR flow
   - Artifact restore (object store snapshot)
   - Restart order
   - Validation gates + smoke tests
   - Rollback decision tree (what to do if validation fails)

8. Runbook: “Restore to a new cluster / new VPC”
   - Bootstrap target cluster
   - Restore control plane
   - Restore artifacts
   - DNS/TLS + cutover checklist
   - Verify API reachability
   - Decommission old cluster guidance

9. On-prem / air-gapped constraints
   - Storage staging repository patterns
   - Offline bundle handling
     - local file bundle backups
     - how to move media (size constraints, chunking?)
   - No external endpoints assumptions
   - Key management patterns (HSM; customer-managed)

D) DR planning + operations
10. DR planning (RPO/RTO guidance)
   - Tiering model: “Standard” vs “Strict”
   - Config recommendations by tier
     - backup frequency
     - retention
     - cross-region replication
   - Cost tradeoffs
   - Restore drill cadence (game days)

11. Observability (metrics, dashboards, alerts)
   - What metrics exist
     - backup success/failure
     - duration percentiles
     - age of last successful backup
     - restore drill outcomes
   - Suggested alert thresholds
   - “Paused clusters” / noise reduction guidance
   - Runbook links conventions (what alerts should link to)
   - Incident-bot shortcuts
     - /backup-status
     - /restore-checklist

12. “Backup before upgrade” policy
   - Required gate: backup create + verify
   - Evidence to attach to change requests
   - Automation hooks (release engineering)

E) Troubleshooting / FAQ
13. Troubleshooting: backup failures
   - Where to look
     - job logs
     - installer logs
     - events
   - Known failure modes
     - AccessDenied / IAM mis-scope
     - storage throttling
     - DB lock contention
     - timeouts
     - partial uploads/checksum mismatches
   - Escalation criteria

14. Troubleshooting: restore issues
   - Restore validation gate failures
   - Maintenance mode stuck / cannot exit
   - PITR mismatch / missing WAL
   - API smoke tests failing

15. Security FAQ
   - “Does Redwood have access to customer keys?”
   - “What does encryption mean here?” (at-rest vs in-transit)
   - “How do you handle audit logging/evidence?”

F) Reference
16. Config reference
   - rw-private-dr flags + config schema (what keys exist)
   - Helm values reference for backup CronJob/restore Job
   - Terraform examples (S3 + KMS wiring; cross-region replication)

17. Appendix
   - Glossary (RPO/RTO, PITR, WAL, maintenance mode)
   - Example IAM policies (least privilege)
   - Example retention policies


Screenshots / diagrams needed (asset checklist)
- [ ] Diagram: end-to-end data flow (backup create -> store -> verify -> restore plan -> execute -> validate)
  - owner: Kira (needs Eng review)
- [ ] Screenshot: Redwood Private Console (if any) showing backup status OR note: “No console surface; use dashboards”
  - open: do we have a console page or strictly Grafana?
- [ ] Screenshot: Grafana dashboard panels
  - backup success rate
  - last successful backup age
  - restore drill annotations
  - owner: Sergio to provide + confirm final panel names
- [ ] Screenshot: example alert (missed backup window) with runbook links
  - owner: Allison/Sergio
- [ ] Terminal snippets (copy/paste friendly)
  - rw-private-dr backup create
  - rw-private-dr backup verify
  - rw-private-dr restore plan
  - rw-private-dr restore execute
  - owner: Connor (confirm flags are stable)
- [ ] YAML snippet: Helm CronJob values example (backup window, timeouts, retries)
  - owner: Diego / Connor
- [ ] Diagram: “maintenance mode” request flow (writes rejected with actionable error)
  - owner: Ethan (confirm semantics)
- [ ] Table: storage backend compatibility matrix (VPC vs on-prem; encryption support)
  - owner: Fatima + Diego to sanity check


Open questions / things we need decisions on (as of 2025-12-18)
1) Naming/branding
- Are we calling it “Day-2 ops toolkit” in customer docs, or “Backup & Restore Toolkit”, or “DR Toolkit”?
- CLI name: `rw-private-dr` vs “Redwood DR CLI” (docs should match binary)

2) What exactly is “protected state” (customer-visible truth table)
- Are we backing up:
  - audit logs? (or just config for export destinations)
  - model artifacts used by runtime nodes? vs only control plane references?
- What about customer-managed secrets/certs? Do we export pointers, or the secrets themselves (ideally not)?

3) PITR prerequisites
- Are we enabling WAL archiving by default, or opt-in?
- How do we document “minimum viable PITR” (storage + retention) without over-promising?

4) Restore to new cluster cutover
- Do we have an official DNS/TLS cutover checklist already, or do we need to create one?
- How do we handle “cluster identity” / licensing if any? (might be sensitive; need confirmation)

5) Air-gapped backups at scale
- What’s our official guidance on bundle size constraints?
  - support chunking? zstd chunk format? (Slack thread suggests debate)
- “Staging repository” definition: NFS share? minio? local disk?

6) Observability canonical sources
- Do we point customers to:
  - Grafana dashboards shipped in observability-pack
  - Prometheus metrics names + example alerts
  - both
- Need final metric names/labels (avoid renames breaking docs)

7) Support boundaries / runbook voice
- Which steps are “must do” vs “nice to do”?
- Where do we say “contact Redwood Support/SE” and what info do we require (logs, job names, backup id)?

8) Backup before upgrade gating
- Do we require “verify” step always, or only for certain upgrade classes?
- What counts as evidence for the change request (screenshot? command output? dashboard panel)?


Draft content notes / reminders to self
- Keep each runbook crisp: Preconditions -> Steps -> Expected result -> Verification -> Rollback -> Troubleshooting.
- Use “Backup ID” and “Snapshot name” consistently. Define once; avoid mixing terms.
- Add “time expectation” callouts (e.g., DB size 200GB, expect ~X min) but make clear it varies.
- Include a “don’t do this” box (e.g., don’t run backup during peak traffic; don’t run overlapping backups).
- Add a “safe defaults” section (recommended schedule + retention) that matches DR tiers.


Proposed doc owners per section (not final)
- Concepts/overview pages: Kira + Elliot (review)
- Architecture/storage targets: Diego + Fatima (review) + Marcus (security review)
- Runbooks: Rafael (SRE), Ethan (control plane hooks), Connor (CLI correctness)
- Observability: Allison + Sergio
- DR planning (RPO/RTO tiers): Miles + Sean + Rafael


Links we should cross-link from
- Private install guide: add “enable scheduled backups” step after install completes
- Upgrade/rollback guide: insert “backup before upgrade” gate
- On-prem packaging docs: add “air-gapped backup constraints” link prominently


Known recent issues to reflect in docs (so we don’t repeat mistakes)
- Permission failures (AccessDenied) during scheduled backups due to missing KMS permissions / bucket policy mismatch
- Restore drill hit permissions issue accessing backup bucket from new cluster (need preflight check)
- Backups running into maintenance window due to timeouts not set realistically for large DBs


Next steps
- [ ] Elliot: confirm final doc IA (1 landing page + 2 concept pages + 3 runbooks + 1 troubleshooting + 1 DR planning + 1 observability)
- [ ] Connor: provide stable CLI help output + example commands (sanitized)
- [ ] Sergio: provide dashboard screenshots + final panel names
- [ ] Marcus/Hanae: review encryption + key handling wording (avoid implying Redwood can decrypt)
- [ ] Fatima: validate air-gapped guidance aligns with real customer environments
- [ ] Rafael: ensure restore validation gates match SRE expectations (what is “must pass”)
